name: Focus and productivity
intro: Where the timer runs in the background and blocking holds, and where it is just a gimmick.

apps.title: Foqos - Tap to Block
apps.verdict: The best distraction blocker in the batch: free, open source, works via NFC or QR code, and physically cuts off your phone with a real-world action. Occasionally a profile deactivates on its own, and the QR scanner breaks on some devices.
apps.loved: Physically scanning an NFC tag to lock the phone creates a far stronger ritual than any in-app button.
apps.weak: The block sometimes disables itself, making the phone accessible without scanning.
apps.whoFor: People with serious phone addiction who need a real physical barrier

quotes.text: I am a UX designer who studied digital detoxing for my masters thesis. I loved the idea of the brick when it came out but the price point is ridiculous. I tried every other app blocker possible and nothing, and I mean NOTHING, worked until foqos. I ordered a 30 pack of nfc stickers for like $10 and

I've never written a review before but this is the app that deserves one. I was about to buy a Brick when I hear about this instead! It does everything I wanted and more, it's intuitive to use, best of all, it's open source and free to use!

apps.title: ATracker Time Tracker
apps.verdict: The best activity tracker in the batch: a single button per task, detailed stats, and a one-time purchase with no subscription, praised by users with years of daily use. Calendar sync is unreliable, and the widget degraded in iOS 18.
apps.loved: One-time purchase with no subscription, plus honest analytics that show where your day actually goes.
apps.weak: After iOS 18 the widget lost the ability to start a task directly from the home screen.
apps.whoFor: Analysts and freelancers who want to know where the day goes

quotes.text: I had the idea to track my activities over time to operationalize my productivity, and to track whether certain productivity strategies I wanted to use were working. This app does everything I needed. Amazing!

apps.title: Countdown Timer Aqua Hourglass
apps.verdict: A visual timer with water filling the screen makes time tangible, especially useful for children with attention difficulties and people with time blindness. The widget, Mac version, and extension beyond one hour do not work for everyone.
apps.loved: The screen filling with water removes the anxiety of numbers and helps feel time without stress.
apps.weak: No way to set a series of back-to-back timers without extra taps.
apps.whoFor: Teachers, parents, and people with ADHD who need a concrete visual time scale

apps.title: Bluebird Focus Timer
apps.verdict: One of the best Pomodoro timers on iPhone: smooth task management, statistics, Apple Watch sync, and correct background operation. The distraction blocker lets individual apps slip through open categories.
apps.loved: The timer keeps running when you switch tasks and does not interrupt your flow with unnecessary prompts.
apps.weak: The app blocker unlocks an entire category when you just need to open one specific app inside it.
apps.whoFor: Students and professionals who need a timer with tasks and stats on iPhone and Watch

apps.title: FocusFlight - Deepfocus Timer
apps.verdict: FocusFlight creates a unique flight atmosphere as a metaphor for focused work and does a good job sustaining motivation, although sync between devices is unstable and the Mac interface can feel sluggish.
apps.loved: An interactive map with a flight route as a visual representation of the work session's progress.
apps.weak: Flight progress does not sync between phone and computer, and there are no short 10-minute sessions.
apps.whoFor: Students and freelancers who want atmosphere, not just a timer

quotes.text: Needs shorter timers (10 min) for people with adhd please this would be amazing

Great job with the 2.0 update. I liked the simplicity of the original app, but the update really differentiates this from other focus apps. I haven't been a fan of other "themed" focus timers because they're often a little too gamified for my taste, but this is perfect - gives me a reason to remembe
I don't know what it is about the airplane noise and buttery feel of the page but top tier focus session's!

apps.title: Focus Tomato - Let's focus now
apps.verdict: The warm retro design with illustrations sets this app apart from faceless minimalist timers, and the core Pomodoro mechanic works reliably. Main limitations: no Live Activities or widgets, and the timer pauses when you switch apps.
apps.loved: The unique vintage character of the interface, with its own atmosphere, makes using the timer feel like a ritual rather than just a tool.
apps.weak: The timer pauses when switching to another app, and there is no widget or Live Activities support for tracking without keeping the screen open.
apps.whoFor: Students and creative people who care about the feel of their workspace

apps.title: FLIP - Focus Timer for Study
apps.verdict: One of the best timers for students: social rooms, hour tracking, daily goals, and an open mode without a forced interval. The app is stable for most users, though it occasionally crashes after updates, and the group task-editing feature needs work.
apps.loved: Group rooms for shared time tracking motivate you to study alongside others and create a social context without distraction.
apps.weak: You cannot edit a goal schedule without fully deleting its history, causing accumulated data to be lost permanently.
apps.whoFor: Students who need motivation through social progress and tracked study hours

apps.title: Session Pomodoro Focus Timer
apps.verdict: A serious Pomodoro tool with session tracking and a site blocker, but the interface is loaded with options and takes a long time to configure. A good fit for people with ADHD who need structure rather than simplicity.
apps.loved: Detailed daily statistics help you see real progress and keep motivation up.
apps.weak: You cannot quickly change session length from the main screen without digging into settings.
apps.whoFor: Productivity enthusiasts who care about time analytics

apps.title: Be Focused – Deep Focus Timer
apps.verdict: A reliable Pomodoro timer with tasks and a widget that genuinely helps maintain a working rhythm. Sync between devices is unreliable, there is no dark mode, and the end-of-session notification is too quiet.
apps.loved: The simple structure of work blocks and breaks lowers resistance before starting a difficult task.
apps.weak: Sync between phone and computer breaks down, and years of data can disappear.
apps.whoFor: Students and workers who need a simple behavioral framework

quotes.text: I find this app, very helpful. It has some great features, and it is free to use. Very helpful for people like me with ADHD that struggle with time management and keeping track of things/time/tasks.

apps.title: Focus Friend, by Hank Green
apps.verdict: A bean that knits while you work and looks upset when you open your phone creates a surprisingly strong emotional loop. App blocking behaves inconsistently, and push notifications break through even with the setting turned off.
apps.loved: The game loop of focus to socks to furniture for the bean motivates people with ADHD better than pure timers do.
apps.weak: Sync between phone and tablet requires manual file transfer, which breaks the entire flow.
apps.whoFor: Young people with ADHD who need an emotional hook

quotes.text: It's a bean. It knits. You open your phone, it gets distracted and drops its work. When it drops their work, they are sad. You have it make socks. You ride the socks in for furniture. Okay, this is actually so fun! The only flaw is that on older iPads, it doesn't register app activity. !!!BUT!!! It

This is literally the only way I've been able to focus in my statistics class this semester. Molly (my focus friend) is so good with helping me keep track of how long I've been working and motivating me to keep going, and the room decor you can buy with socks is super cute!

apps.title: Flow: Focus & Pomodoro Timer
apps.verdict: One of the best Pomodoro timers in the App Store, with a clean design, focus sounds, and cross-device sync. The core mechanic is solid, though Live Activities sometimes disappear and the site blocker has to be configured separately on each device.
apps.loved: Sessions sync between iPhone and Mac, and the distracting-site blocker holds until the timer ends with no easy way around it.
apps.weak: App blocking on iPhone can be bypassed by force-quitting, and block lists do not sync between devices automatically.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who seriously works with the Pomodoro technique on Mac and iPhone

apps.title: Focus To-Do: Focus Timer&Tasks
apps.verdict: Focus To-Do combines Pomodoro with a full task planner and works well for people who need a system rather than just a timer, though widget bugs and task-logic issues have accumulated in recent versions.
apps.loved: Sync across phone, browser, and desktop inside one working system.
apps.weak: Widgets show wrong data, and tasks occasionally duplicate or reschedule themselves to the next day on their own.
apps.whoFor: People who need a Pomodoro timer inside a full-featured task planner

quotes.text: I have to say after trying many things this app is working for me as a ADHD person who struggled throughout your life. It does induce sense of urgency for work which leads to completion. I like the tasks feature as well as it keeps you organized as well.

apps.title: Emphasis: Flow & Focus Timer
apps.verdict: A beautiful Pomodoro timer with solid Apple Watch and iPhone sync, a clean interface, and accumulated session history. Version 8.0 broke stability for some users, and moving all functionality behind a subscription upset longtime buyers.
apps.loved: Apple Watch sync works without lag, and the timer runs in the background correctly.
apps.weak: Stats do not let you view total time spent on a specific task over an arbitrary date range.
apps.whoFor: Productive Apple users who want a beautiful and reliable Pomodoro timer

apps.title: Focus Quest: Study buddy
apps.verdict: A rare case where RPG mechanics genuinely motivate studying rather than becoming a distraction in themselves. Some ADHD users report 2-3 hour sessions without getting sidetracked. The risk: the game can pull you in harder than the task itself.
apps.loved: Character progression turns every study session into tangible movement toward a goal.
apps.weak: The game loop is deep enough to become its own source of distraction instead of the task.
apps.whoFor: Students and people with ADHD who are motivated by RPG rewards rather than a bare timer

apps.title: Brick - Ditch Distractions
apps.verdict: A physical dongle, an NFC fob, as the unlock mechanism creates a real barrier against impulsively picking up the phone, and it honestly works where purely software solutions give in. The decision to remove the timed session feature without a replacement frustrated loyal users and reduced everyday flexibility.
apps.loved: The physical ritual of touching the fob breaks the automatic reflex far better than an on-screen warning.
apps.weak: Quick session-by-duration launch was removed, leaving only scheduling, which does not work for unpredictable days.
apps.whoFor: People with serious phone addiction who are willing to carry a fob

quotes.text: I find that Brick is straightforward, easy to use, and not at all overwhelming! For me, the best part is the physical component. Once the set schedule ends, you have to actually get up and tap the phone to unlock it. Since it isn't a passive timer that just hands back access, I find that this preser

I have loved this product, but I spoke with customer service and how they removed the scheduling feature while on the go. This is a dealbreaker when some of us can't foresee our schedules constantly changing and don't travel with the dongle.

apps.title: FocusPomo · Pomodoro Timer
apps.verdict: An honest Pomodoro with tomato-themed gamification, stable performance, and a pleasant look. End-of-session notifications are sometimes silent, and category-level stats are limited.
apps.loved: The visual tomato counter motivates you not to break the session.
apps.weak: No breakdown of time by category for a given day or week.
apps.whoFor: Students and remote workers who need a simple, enjoyable Pomodoro

quotes.text: It's really simple and seeing the changed color fruit when you fail to complete a session really helps keep yourself accountable. Very nice :)

apps.title: Focus Traveller - Flow Timer
apps.verdict: A beautiful travel concept and flexible timer mode selection, Pomodoro, fixed, or open-ended, make this one of the most pleasant timers around. The timer pauses when you switch apps, and the cumulative counter stops accumulating for some users.
apps.loved: The cozy travel aesthetic and built-in playlist selector remove every reason not to start.
apps.weak: The timer pauses whenever you switch apps, making it useless for working across multiple apps at once.
apps.whoFor: People studying at home who want a beautiful environment for their sessions

quotes.text: I like the graphics and the journey concept. Dislike that I can't totally silence the app's background sounds without muting my phone. And the timer/app pauses and eventually shuts down if I do any additional action whatsoever on the phone besides start the timer and set the phone aside. It's bizarr

apps.title: one sec | screen time + focus
apps.verdict: A minimalist mindfulness tool: before opening a blocked app you take a deep breath or do a short exercise, which genuinely breaks autopilot and reduces social media use. The weak point is that the free tier blocks only one app, making it nearly useless when you need to limit several social networks.
apps.loved: A pause before Instagram breaks the conditioned reflex better than a hard block. Several reviews describe real habit change within weeks.
apps.weak: Hard blocking is easy to bypass even in the paid version, and one app on the free tier is far too few.
apps.whoFor: People who want to mindfully cut back on social media rather than block it by force

quotes.text: It sounds trite, but this app absolutely changed my life for the better. I have effectively cut out all social media except for one website that I allow. This app effectively broke the muscle memory habit of opening up Instagram or other endless scrolling apps whenever I had a free moment or picked
It does the job. Just making me take a moment and asking "Do you really need to took at this site? Do you need to do it NOW?" is enough of a prompt to stop my mind from wandering.
I had a bad habit of doom scrolling Instagram and even LinkedIn (lol). I just started using this app yesterday, and I already am no longer reflexively hopping on the app.

It's a great app. But it triggered too easily. I sometimes want to turn off dnd or something in the control center and re triggered it. If intential app switching is going to be under the pro version, then at least allow small out of app access like using flashlight or accessing control center to no

Overall, this app has helped me stay away from Instagram for some amount of time. What I've come to strongly dislike is the inability as a free user to turn off haptics for the breathing intervention. I get stressed by haptics and turn them off whenever possible, and I'm not in a condition to be abl
This is the only app that has truly had an impact on reducing my doom scrolling and I'm so grateful!

apps.title: Flora - Green Focus
apps.verdict: A gamified timer with real tree planting as a reward for focus. The mechanic works well for motivation, but app blocking is unreliable on iPad, the interface degraded after replacing illustrations with AI art, and coins and progress are sometimes lost.
apps.loved: The idea of growing real trees for time away from your phone hooks users and keeps them engaged longer than any plain timer.
apps.weak: The app whitelist works intermittently, and there is no cross-platform connection between iOS and Android.
apps.whoFor: Students who need game-like motivation for studying

quotes.text: I love this app. It's so cute growing different plants especially since I can keep a real plant alive. But it also helps me stay focused and busy since I want to grow my plants. Still trying to figure it out but I like it so far. I wish I could see all the different plants I've finished or killed bu

apps.title: MultiTimer: Multiple timers
apps.verdict: MultiTimer handles running several independent timers at once and has served users faithfully for years, but notifications are unreliable on a locked screen and when the app is in the background.
apps.loved: Multiple named timers on one screen running in parallel without confusion.
apps.weak: The alert does not fire when the phone is on silent or the app is backgrounded.
apps.whoFor: People juggling multiple parallel processes: cooking, workouts, pets

apps.title: Brain.fm: Focus & Sleep Music
apps.verdict: The neuroscience genuinely works for part of the audience, especially people with ADHD. Several users write about a noticeable effect after months of daily use. A weak frontend and an unstable player, playback errors and dropped tracks, undercut the experience.
apps.loved: The high-neural-effect mode helps people with ADHD sustain attention where regular music fails.
apps.weak: The player periodically crashes with a playback error, and the interface gives no sense of what is happening inside.
apps.whoFor: People with ADHD who need background sound without lyrics

quotes.text: I've been using Brain.fm for almost 2 years now and I can't recommend it enough for those with ADHD or just generally have trouble focusing on tasks. Personally I find regular music too distracting and silence makes my brain too loud. Brain.fm is a great equalizer with music that prevents my brain f
closest thing to superpowers for attention deficit ppl

apps.title: Be Focused Pro - Focus Timer
apps.verdict: A solid Pomodoro timer with convenient task-zone breakdown, but sync between devices is spotty. Long-term users stick around, while newer ones increasingly leave because of lost data and broken notifications.
apps.loved: Flexible session-to-task and GTD zone mapping helps you see exactly where the day goes.
apps.weak: Sync between iPhone, iPad, and Mac is unreliable: data can disappear, and historical stats vanish after re-login.
apps.whoFor: GTD enthusiasts and structured time-tracking fans

apps.title: ChickFocus: Pomodoro Timer
apps.verdict: The chicken-and-farm game mechanic genuinely keeps users in sessions, and the overlay countdown widget is handy when working on an iPad. The app whitelist sometimes fails, and there is still no dark mode in 2025.
apps.loved: The visible chick that dies if you leave the app creates an emotional attachment that keeps you in a session better than any timer.
apps.weak: No home-screen countdown widget, which causes ADHD users to lose track of time remaining.
apps.whoFor: School students and university students motivated by game-like rewards rather than plain numbers

apps.title: Freedom: Screen Time Control
apps.verdict: One of the few blockers with cross-device sync and a hard mode that actually works. The VPN layer can slow down the internet or conflict with other apps, and iOS settings allow the block to be bypassed.
apps.loved: The hard mode with one unlock per week removes the escape hatch for weak moments.
apps.weak: The VPN layer periodically slows down apps you actually need and conflicts with other services.
apps.whoFor: Adults with serious phone addiction who need a reliable multi-device barrier

quotes.text: This is the BEST tool for blocking individual websites. I've tried them all, and Freedom wins hands-down! I love the "hard-mode" blocking function that only allows an emergency unblock once every seven days. The interface is simple and easy to understand (and doesn't change all the time and confuse

On iOS, it's very easy to simply turn off Freedom's Screen Time access during a session and regain access to blocked apps. The Freedom Profile VPN doesn't fully compensate. For example, I can regain access to YouTube in seconds, even with the VPN blocking the domain.

apps.title: Forest: Focus for Productivity
apps.verdict: The classic focus timer with a virtual forest gamification and real tree planting: the mechanic works, the design is pleasant. The weak point is the shift to a subscription that upset paying users, monthly challenges occasionally fail to register, and data was lost for some users after a forced account sign-out.
apps.loved: Not wanting to kill the tree keeps you at your desk longer than any act of willpower.
apps.weak: Monthly challenges are buggy, pausing the timer now requires a subscription, and stats sometimes do not match actual sessions.
apps.whoFor: Students and freelancers who need visual motivation with a minimalist timer

quotes.text: I've studied for an hour straight just so I can have cuter plants

I love this app! It helps me focus when I practice my instruments sometimes when I am bored I will just make a timer to watch it grow it pass passes the time and I have gotten better with my instruments!

I love this app a lot! I have severe ADHD and struggle with time management. I love the events they do and the fact that I can plant a cute little tree every time i set a timer! I love it so much that i got an annual subscription!

apps.title: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker
apps.verdict: Routinery guides you through the steps of a routine well and helps with time blindness, but an update broke basic navigation between tasks, and notifications can bombard you at the wrong moments.
apps.loved: The sequential one-task-now mode removes anxiety from a long to-do list.
apps.weak: Navigation between steps is rigid: skipping one step automatically closes all the ones before it.
apps.whoFor: People who struggle with planning their morning and evening

apps.title: Focus Town: Study With Friends
apps.verdict: The cozy visual atmosphere and shared sessions genuinely help some users sit down to study. Phone-number registration locks out users whose country is not supported, and the music cuts out periodically.
apps.loved: The virtual cafe and the presence of other students create a sense of working together and reduce procrastination.
apps.weak: Music drops out several times a week and support does not respond to reports.
apps.whoFor: School and university students who need the feeling of not studying alone

quotes.text: Adding a chat feature to the sessions is a massive step backward. We are here to focus, have a drive and reason to put phone down, not to socialize. This isn't a feature it's a distraction that defeats the entire objective of the session.

apps.title: Study Time With Rain: Pomodoro
apps.verdict: A cozy rain-and-ASMR atmosphere creates a pleasant study context, and the basic Pomodoro with background sounds is available for free. The same complaint appears from every user: sound and timer stop when you leave the app, breaking any multi-app workflow.
apps.loved: Library ASMR and rain sounds create a sense of someone nearby, which especially helps people with ADHD.
apps.weak: The timer and background sound stop when you switch to another app, making it impossible to work across multiple apps at once.
apps.whoFor: Students who need a cozy sound environment to get absorbed in studying

apps.title: Focus Tree: Timer & Flashcards
apps.verdict: The garden gamification genuinely motivates students to study, and the built-in flashcards work. However the timer records time incorrectly, and adding AI features has hurt stability and design.
apps.loved: A shared garden with friends creates a live social incentive not to abandon the session.
apps.weak: The time tracker occasionally logs wrong data and loses earned coins.
apps.whoFor: School and university students who need game-like motivation for studying

apps.title: Detox - Digital Detox App
apps.verdict: The blocker works harder than iOS Screen Time and genuinely cuts social media use by a large factor. The absence of a scheduled block by time of day limits flexibility.
apps.loved: The five-minute forced limit after time runs out is strict enough to break the habit loop.
apps.weak: No way to automatically enable a block on a schedule, for example overnight.
apps.whoFor: Adults who find iOS Screen Time too easy to bypass and need a real barrier

apps.title: Refocus: Block Apps & Websites
apps.verdict: Refocus blocks apps and creates real friction before opening distracting sources, but hard mode is paid-only and the free block is too easy to override on your own.
apps.loved: The friction when trying to open a blocked app genuinely breaks autopilot.
apps.weak: In free mode it is too easy to unblock yourself, which defeats the whole point of the restriction.
apps.whoFor: People who want to break the habit of automatically opening social media

quotes.text: I like this app as it helps with unconscious opening of apps and whatnot. I do wish you could enable it without being able disable it but that's locked behind a paid tier.

apps.title: AppBlock: Block Apps & Website
apps.verdict: A rich set of blocking rules and schedules, but automatic schedule-based triggering regularly breaks and requires a manual restart. Strict mode can be bypassed through Apple settings.
apps.loved: Flexible schedules and geofences give precise control over app access.
apps.weak: Schedule-based auto-blocking does not always fire and requires manual refresh.
apps.whoFor: People with ADHD who want strict but configurable screen control

quotes.text: I have ADHD and absolutely no concept of time. I'll scroll all day and have no idea it's been hours. This app gives me so many options to limit my screen time.

First off, I want to say that the people who have been emailing are lovely. But I want to point out that even on strict mode, you are able to go into Apple settings- apps- AppBlock- and disable screentime permissions. To do this you don't need an Apple screentime code, OR a code from app block.

apps.title: YPT - Study Group
apps.verdict: A social study community with time tracking and competitive elements that genuinely motivates studying alongside friends. Technical issues after updates, freezes, and offline mode failures reduce reliability.
apps.loved: Shared competitive study-time tracking with friends creates real mutual motivation that a solo timer cannot provide.
apps.weak: After updates, offline mode, app blocking, and data sync regularly break, making the app an unreliable daily tool.
apps.whoFor: School and university students who value studying with friends and group dynamics

apps.title: No Scroll - Limit Screen Time
apps.verdict: The slow-down mechanic before opening an app works better than standard iOS limits: users genuinely cut time on social media. The block schedule sometimes freezes and does not lift on time.
apps.loved: Having to confirm intent before entering an app creates a pause that is often enough to change your mind.
apps.weak: Schedule-based blocking keeps running past the set period with no quick way to lift it.
apps.whoFor: People who want doomscrolling to be intentional rather than automatic

apps.title: Timer+ Countdown & Stopwatch
apps.verdict: A multi-timer with support for several simultaneous countdowns and task labels, reliably used for years in the kitchen and at the gym. A recurring audio and volume-conflict issue with ads appears and disappears across updates, and the basic alert sometimes fails to fire in the background.
apps.loved: Multiple named timers running simultaneously on one screen, convenient for cooking and workouts.
apps.weak: The alert does not always sound when the app is backgrounded, and ads interrupt the volume of external audio.
apps.whoFor: People juggling several tasks with different timers

quotes.text: I've been using this app for a few years and every so often there is an issue with audio ducking. It seems that certain ads have an effect on the audio volume when alarms go off, many times, lately, the volume does not return to its original level, requiring the app to be closed and reopened.

apps.title: Repeat Timer: Interval Remind
apps.verdict: The repeat timer works, but background mode is unstable: the app freezes if you leave the screen or lock the phone. Live Activities visually freeze.
apps.loved: Convenient for workouts and cooking with multiple stages.
apps.weak: Cannot maintain a session in the background without keeping the screen on.
apps.whoFor: Coaches and cooks who keep the phone in view at all times

quotes.text: It doesn't allow you to stream apps while counting down…even with the background permission…you have to be IN the app in order for the timer to continue counting down…and the phone can't be locked…stupid…

apps.title: Focus Hero: Goals & Habits
apps.verdict: The RPG gamification of focus is an interesting idea, and several users say it was what made deep work a habit for them. Combat mechanics are buggy, progress occasionally resets completely, and the reward system loses meaning without access to adventure mode.
apps.loved: The RPG loop of focus to coins to gear to battle motivates where a plain timer bores you within a day.
apps.weak: Progress and equipment periodically reset completely with no explanation.
apps.whoFor: Gamers and fantasy fans who need narrative motivation

apps.title: Focus Keeper - Pomodoro Timer
apps.verdict: A long-lived Pomodoro timer that gradually accumulated features until it lost focus: a mandatory multi-screen onboarding, a freezing home-screen widget, and no cross-device sync despite a paid subscription. The core 25/5 mechanic works but is buried under layers of new interface.
apps.loved: Once configured, the simple Pomodoro rhythm with ambient sound genuinely keeps you in the flow.
apps.weak: Multi-screen onboarding cannot be skipped, and the home-screen widget periodically freezes.
apps.whoFor: Patient Pomodoro users willing to work through the setup

quotes.text: I like that in addition to the timer they provide some background noise to help you keep focused.
you flooded this app with unnecessary features and premium. it's a timer.

I miss when apps just did what they advertise. I remember using this app back in the day as a useful simple timer app to track study sessions. Downloaded it today and it bombards you with 10 minutes of survey questions and bloat, constant popups. Just give me a goddamn timer, stop trying to farm me

apps.title: Pomodoro - Focus Timer
apps.verdict: Pomodoro Focus Timer is simple and clear for basic use but has accumulated regressions: some users see their sound settings reset after updates, the timer fails to notify in the background, and Watch integration is unstable.
apps.loved: Minimalism with no extra screens, session starts in literally one tap.
apps.weak: The timer does not notify when the app is not in focus, making it an unreliable tool.
apps.whoFor: People who need a quick Pomodoro with no settings or statistics

quotes.text: It is fairly simple to use, but if the app does not have focus, it does not bother to notify you of when the timer is up. This is a major drawback.

apps.title: Pond - Screen Time & Pomodoro
apps.verdict: The former Focus Keeper with a clean interface and configurable Pomodoro rhythm. After the rebrand and the addition of screen-time data access it lost trust from part of its audience, and the timer started stopping in the background for some users.
apps.loved: Clean minimalist interface with the ability to set each phase length without extra screens.
apps.weak: The timer stops when you switch to another app or lock the screen, making background counting unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Classic Pomodoro fans with no interest in social features or gamification

apps.title: Power Focus - Work Break Timer
apps.verdict: A simple Pomodoro timer with a minimal interface that runs stably on the phone. The hourly alert does not fire on a locked screen, and the Watch app periodically loses sync.
apps.loved: Configuring session and break lengths without extra screens makes starting instant.
apps.weak: The timer does not switch to break mode automatically if the screen turns off or a call comes in.
apps.whoFor: People who want a minimalist Pomodoro with no subscriptions and no extra features

apps.title: Focus@Will: Control Your ADD
apps.verdict: The music genuinely induces flow and helps with ADHD, but the mobile app has been effectively abandoned: Bluetooth does not work, tracks loop, and support does not respond. Value remains only in the web version.
apps.loved: Music channels tuned to brain type noticeably speed up entry into deep focus.
apps.weak: The mobile app is not updated: playback cuts out, Bluetooth is broken, and the track library loops.
apps.whoFor: People working at a computer who are happy to listen through a browser rather than their phone

apps.title: Endel: Focus & Sleep Sounds
apps.verdict: Generative audio background for focus and sleep with beautiful visuals, but the promotional videos feature tracks that are not in the app, the 120-dollar-a-year subscription does not show up in Apple subscriptions and is hard to cancel, and audio interrupts on notifications. Works genuinely for some ADHD users.
apps.loved: The adaptive soundscape noticeably improves concentration for neurodivergent people, according to several independent reviews.
apps.weak: Sound stops on any call or notification and requires manual restart, which is fatal for meditation and sleep.
apps.whoFor: People with ADHD who benefit from a continuous background sound stream for work or sleep

quotes.text: For someone neurodivergent, this has become a serious boon for my cognitive functions, specifically focus. I focus better during work, creativity, and exercise.

apps.title: Cape: App to Pause Excess
apps.verdict: Cape hides apps and partially works on a schedule, but location-based scheduling is unreliable, and after updates hidden apps sometimes fail to return or, conversely, fail to disappear.
apps.loved: Automatic hiding of work apps at home with no manual intervention.
apps.weak: Schedule and geolocation triggers often do not fire on time without manually opening the app.
apps.whoFor: People who want to separate a work profile from a personal one on their phone

quotes.text: This app is a sanity saver. It allows me to automatically block work apps when I'm at home. If my younger children want to play in my phone I can block all apps including those calls that you dread having to explain how your three year old just called your boss at 6 am and you had no clue.

apps.title: Flipd: focus & study timer
apps.verdict: The social co-studying aspect works and motivates, but the timer crashes after the first break, stats show wrong time, and Safari blocking is broken after an update.
apps.loved: Virtual co-study rooms create a sense of presence.
apps.weak: The timer is unstable: crashes on breaks and loses session data.
apps.whoFor: Students who need a social push to study

quotes.text: This is a great app it is now my favorite studying app. It has helped me to focus and buckle down and study! It has also helped with my short attention span my favorite feature is being able to study with other people in the silent study groups. Download it! You won't regret it great for college stu
Love this app and the idea, really helps me focus when a timer is running and other people are "studying with me". Love the music and stats feature.

This is unacceptable. You don't allow free users to pause more than once while on a timer? And you only allow limits of 40 minutes at a time when free apps have it unlimited? That's wrong. And I have verified myself your so called " real time studying together" people count is fake……why do you h

So, i'll start by saying I generally love this app, there is 1 thing keeping me from buying the year pass actually. That one thing is that the weekly stats are completely wrong, I'm not studying at 1 am, and the chart keeps saying that's when i'm studying, when you look at the stuff individually, no

apps.title: Focus - Timer for Productivity
apps.verdict: A stylish Pomodoro timer with a good concept and visual execution that falls short on technical details: Watch vibration notifications miss sessions, widgets conflict with timer controls, and settings resetting on every launch is annoying. Potential is there, stability is not.
apps.loved: A clean interface and Shortcuts integration help weave Pomodoro into a real workflow.
apps.weak: Apple Watch vibration notifications fire unpredictably, and adding a widget to the screen breaks timer controls inside the app.
apps.whoFor: Apple ecosystem users who want Pomodoro with Shortcuts integration

apps.title: Aqimo: Salah Focus
apps.verdict: Same concept as Prayr: block the phone during prayer with reminders. The basic mechanic works, but blocking stops functioning after updates and there are very few reviews confirming stable long-term operation.
apps.loved: The simple idea of blocking the phone between prayers is immediately clear and works during the trial period.
apps.weak: App blocking periodically stops working after updates, leaving paying users without a functional tool.
apps.whoFor: Muslims who need a forced phone break during prayer time

apps.title: Repeat Timer
apps.verdict: A simple repeating timer with a responsive developer, but the core task of an audio alert on Apple Watch in the background is unreliable. The screen has to stay active or the alert disappears.
apps.loved: The developer fixes breakages after iOS updates quickly and replies to emails.
apps.weak: The timer does not alert on Apple Watch when the app is backgrounded or the screen is locked.
apps.whoFor: People who train with intervals and are comfortable keeping the screen active

apps.title: Time Timer
apps.verdict: Time Timer wins on its visual representation of shrinking time, but basic alert reliability suffers: sound disappears on a locked screen, during incoming calls, and when running in the background.
apps.loved: A clear visual disc that physically shows how much time remains.
apps.weak: The alert fires unpredictably: sometimes silent, sometimes at the wrong time, sometimes four beeps instead of continuous.
apps.whoFor: Teachers and parents who need a clear visual timer for children

quotes.text: It is one of the most important things for me with Pomodoro timers. I NEED to hear time ticking to get pressured to work and no to get distracted additionally by looking every few minutes how much more I have to finish the task or until the time expires.

Used this for a couple times until I realized the fatal flaw. Whatever time you select should be A WHOLE CIRCLE. If you set the timer for an hour, the circle should represent an hour. But if you set the timer for a half an hour., The circle should represent a half hour. That way you can visually see

apps.title: Stay Focused App/Site Blocker
apps.verdict: An app blocker with profiles and a strict mode that helps some ADHD users limit social media, but strict mode can be bypassed by rebooting the phone or entering iOS settings, making the tool unreliable. Forced rating prompts inside the app are annoying.
apps.loved: The extra step required to bypass the block already creates enough resistance to keep you from reflexively reaching for the phone.
apps.weak: Strict mode is not protected against a device reboot bypass, which defeats it for users with strong addiction.
apps.whoFor: Adults with ADHD who need a soft barrier against social media during working hours

apps.title: Bento: Calm Focus Timer
apps.verdict: The three-task-in-boxes concept worked well in the simpler version, but the redesign added clutter and broke what people loved about the app. Background music with no way to turn it off and stale updates undermine trust.
apps.loved: The bento method and Japanese aesthetic help you focus on three key tasks without anxiety.
apps.weak: After the redesign the app lost its main advantage, simplicity, and now feels like an overloaded task manager.
apps.whoFor: People looking for a visually pleasant focus timer without extras

apps.title: Opal: Screen Time Control
apps.verdict: Before the major update Opal was one of the best distraction blockers, with a clean interface and real results, but the redesign made navigation chaotic, weakened blocking, and put basic features behind a paywall. The product is currently in a transitional crisis.
apps.loved: The old version genuinely reduced screen time. Several users report dropping from 7 to 2 hours a day.
apps.weak: After the update blocking became bypassable, the interface is confusing, and the focus-hours widget is broken.
apps.whoFor: People still on the old version or willing to wait for fixes

quotes.text: This has always been a wonderful app for me. I only have the free version, and it has radically decreased my screen time. I struggle with compulsive phone use, but the long waiting times for breaks really helped me think about what I was doing.

This is a great app. Beautiful, functional, and useful. But I just don't get some of the changes. Why is this not on the iPad and Mac as a universal app? I know there is a Mac app but why no iPad? Universal would still be nice. The latest major version also added unblock a single app…but with blocke

apps.title: Blank Spaces Launcher
apps.verdict: Blank Spaces Launcher gives a minimalist screen free of temptation and works for some users, but setup is complex, widgets lost their clean look in iOS with Liquid Glass, and blocking resets on its own periodically.
apps.loved: An empty home screen with only the icons you need physically removes triggers for autopilot app-opening.
apps.weak: Blocking disables itself periodically, and once reset it cannot be re-enabled without recreating the setup.
apps.whoFor: People who want to hide apps from sight rather than block them at the system level

quotes.text: From the moment I downloaded it, my screen time immediately plummeted. I started spending more time in the present moment, enjoying my family, and my life. That was a couple of months ago. I never spend money on apps (just on principle), but let me tell you, I bought a lifetime subscription as fast

This app is the only one that was actually effective enough to curb my
phone addiction!! I am so incredibly happy with how much progress this app has allowed me to make, and I recommend it to anyone struggling with social media / phone addiction.

All it does is replace the Home Screen but you can still access all your apps with a simple search. Very buggy. Company says 100% guaranteed satisfaction upon purchase but doesn't respond to requests of refunds so I had to go through Apple to get one

This app is best because it lets you lock the app and do 1 of like 5 things. Either do a breathing excerise , passcode, do push-ups (camera has to be on ikr ? Haha) and even touch grass (you have to take a pic of grass lol) literally the app is perfect so if you need help getting off of tiktok lol T

I love this app, but one little gap keeps me from perfection. It seems that your steak only counts days that you trigger the blank app mechanism but if the goal is reduced usage, it's a downer to reset my count on a day that I've avoided those apps completely.

apps.title: Zen Flip Clock - Minimal Timer
apps.verdict: Beautiful flip-clock visuals and a widget, but the Pomodoro resets when you switch apps or lock the screen, and the timer is interrupted by rating requests right in the middle of a session.
apps.loved: The minimalist design with digit-flip animation looks good on screen.
apps.weak: Pomodoro resets when you leave the app or when the battery runs low.
apps.whoFor: People who want attractive desk-style clocks and do not rely on background timer operation

quotes.text: Pomodoro resets every time you switch apps or lock the screen.

apps.title: Bakery - Study Timer
apps.verdict: The cute baked-goods reward concept for sessions is motivating and pulls people back to the app, but a critical sign-in error makes the app completely inaccessible to a significant portion of new users, and the developer has not pushed an update in over two years.
apps.loved: A game-style pastry collection earned through study sessions creates tangible accumulation that genuinely draws you back to your desk.
apps.weak: Progress and the pastry collection reset without warning, and accumulated study hours vanish permanently.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers and students motivated by visual reward accumulation

apps.title: Productive - Habit Tracker
apps.verdict: A habit tracker with a tidy design and reminders, but the timer does not work in the background, cross-device sync has been removed, and the paywall appears at the very start of onboarding. The core action of marking a habit complete is awkward.
apps.loved: A clean interface and widget motivate you to return to the list every day.
apps.weak: The goal timer stops when the app is minimized, there is no sync, and adding or editing a habit is cumbersome.
apps.whoFor: Beginners in habit tracking on a single device

quotes.text: This would be an amazing app, except the goal timer feature doesn't keep time if the app is not in focus! Many apps nowadays have timers that still work in background, this just feels like a lazy throwback to smartphones from 10 years ago.

apps.title: Brainrot: Screen Time Control
apps.verdict: Brainrot has an attractive and motivating design, but app blocking does not activate automatically on schedule without manually launching the app, which defeats the entire self-restriction mechanism.
apps.loved: Brain health gamification expressed as a percentage creates a real emotional stake.
apps.weak: Blocking does not turn on without opening the app. The user has to remember to do it every day.
apps.whoFor: Young people who want to control social media time through a game mechanic

apps.title: Trello: Daily Task Tracker
apps.verdict: A kanban board for tasks, not a timer or focus blocker. The mobile app is chronically slow and loses sync, making it barely usable as a productivity tool on the phone.
apps.loved: Flexible board structure suits complex projects.
apps.weak: The mobile version lags and desyncs even with just three boards.
apps.whoFor: Teams that work primarily in the web version

apps.title: OffScreen: Screen Time Control
apps.verdict: A nice interface and gentle reminders appeal to users, but app blocking reliably breaks, schedules delete themselves, and tracking only works with the app open. The core screen-control function does not work.
apps.loved: Non-intrusive motivating notifications genuinely helped people reduce phone time without feeling forced.
apps.weak: App blocking stops working after updates, schedules reset on their own, and the timer requires the app to stay open.
apps.whoFor: People who want to reduce phone dependence but not for hard control

quotes.text: I play Spotify while I'm workin, so it says I've been on my phone ten hours a day when that's not accurate at all. Which we could select apps that "don't count"

apps.title: Prayr - Salah & Focus
apps.verdict: The app sets up phone blocking before prayer and helps users not miss prayers. Users who bought access report it works. However nearly all functionality is behind a paywall with no meaningful free mode.
apps.loved: Blocks distracting apps until the prayer is finished and genuinely helps maintain the prayer schedule.
apps.weak: No Shia prayer-time calculation methods, narrowing the audience.
apps.whoFor: Practicing Muslims willing to pay for prayer discipline

apps.title: Blok — Screen Time Blocker
apps.verdict: The physical card-slot mechanic is an interesting idea, but block scheduling behaves unpredictably and support is unhelpful. Strong concept, rough execution.
apps.loved: The physical barrier genuinely makes it harder to pick up the phone and doomscroll.
apps.weak: Block scheduling is unreliable: blocks do not lift after a break, and manual control is buggy.
apps.whoFor: People who want to physically set down the phone rather than just set a limit

apps.title: BlockSite: Block Apps & Focus
apps.verdict: Blocks sites and apps, but the VPN layer sometimes interferes with services you actually need. The free tier is nearly nonexistent: even a 7-day schedule requires a subscription.
apps.loved: Works on iOS without complex setup and blocks the sites you target.
apps.weak: The VPN-based blocking method periodically cuts access to services you need.
apps.whoFor: Users who want to block one or two distracting sites without complexity

apps.title: Study Bunny: Focus Timer
apps.verdict: A cute study timer with a rabbit character and a session-point system. The idea is motivating and works for younger users, but ads appear on every tap and interrupt the music, completely destroying the work flow. Without purchasing ad removal the app is counterproductive.
apps.loved: The virtual pet and reward shop keep teenagers studying better than a plain timer.
apps.weak: Ads appear every time you switch tabs and interrupt background music, the top complaint across reviews.
apps.whoFor: School and university students who have bought ad removal

quotes.text: The app is super good it helped me study a lot because I want to buy stuff for my bunny

apps.title: Cub: Self Care Pet & Focus
apps.verdict: The tamagotchi-pet concept for self-discipline is appealing, but the app is technically unstable: items disappear, progress resets, streaks clear without warning. Too few product mechanics are available without a subscription.
apps.loved: The small panda you care for creates attachment and the desire to return every day.
apps.weak: Purchased and found items regularly disappear, which destroys the meaning of the reward system.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers who enjoy the tamagotchi aesthetic and caring for a virtual pet

quotes.text: No clue what happened, but my entire app and cub reset itself after 6 months into using the app. I lost my progress (level 20) and my log and everything overnight without warning. I am frustrated but not heartbroken. With my childhood tamagotchi experience, I only mourn for 5 minutes and started ove

apps.title: Focus timer - time keeper
apps.verdict: A minimalist timer with a clean display, but with unsafe ads in the free version and a timer that stops when you switch to another app. The app has not been updated in a long time and the key shortcomings remain.
apps.loved: A clean large single-mode display helps concentration if the device is dedicated solely to the timer.
apps.weak: The timer pauses when switching to another app, making background operation impossible.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who needs a simple attractive timer on a dedicated screen

apps.title: Liberate - Website Blocker
apps.verdict: A simple site blocker for Safari that worked well before iOS 18 and now fails to block for most users. The developer has not updated the app in over two years and does not respond to reports.
apps.loved: Before iOS 18 it worked without complex setup and held the set timer with no way to reset it.
apps.weak: Works only in Safari and is easily bypassed through other browsers or by disabling the extension in Settings.
apps.whoFor: Safari users on iOS before version 18 who need a simple one-shot barrier

apps.title: BlockerX Pro: Content Blocker
apps.verdict: An accountability-based blocker that works when it does not crash, but instability and iOS limitations make it unreliable. Scheduled blocks regularly fail to start or stop on time.
apps.loved: The accountability-partner mechanic, where a partner can approve or reject an unblock request, genuinely raises the cost of bypassing restrictions.
apps.weak: Block scheduling is unreliable: it often fails to turn on or off at the right time.
apps.whoFor: People fighting content addiction who need external accountability

apps.title: VibeAlarm
apps.verdict: The idea of a vibration-only timer with no sound is useful in meetings and workouts, but the execution fails: the timer stops when the screen locks and resets when you leave the app. The core feature does not work in the core scenario.
apps.loved: A silent vibration alert with no sound is perfect for discreet time control during presentations or public speaking.
apps.weak: The timer stops when the screen locks and does not run in the background, making the app useless in most real situations.
apps.whoFor: Speakers and coaches who need a silent cue right in their hand

apps.title: Mars Craft - Focus Build Timer
apps.verdict: The Mars colony concept growing from focus sessions is original, but the app is technically unstable: progress is lost on crashes, maps fail to load, and support is unresponsive. Feels like an abandoned project.
apps.loved: The idea of building a Mars base in exchange for real phone-free time creates a genuine charge for the first few sessions.
apps.weak: Crashing during a session resets progress, and the developers do not respond to reports.
apps.whoFor: Space enthusiasts willing to tolerate an unstable app for the concept

apps.title: Fullscreen Clock: Flip & Focus
apps.verdict: Essentially just a large digital clock face, and it does even that poorly: the widget does not update the time zone during daylight saving transitions, and ads cover the screen even after purchase. Not suitable as a focus work timer.
apps.loved: A large readable full-screen display with different styles is convenient as a desk clock on a tablet.
apps.weak: Ads interrupt use even for paying users, and the widget does not switch time zones automatically.
apps.whoFor: People who need a large desk clock on a spare device

apps.title: Focus - Userscripts & Player
apps.verdict: Based on reviews this is a browser with userscript support, not a focus timer. Scripts break after updates, pages fail to load, and the core function is unstable.
apps.loved: The idea of running userscripts directly in a mobile browser appeals to a technical audience.
apps.weak: Scripts stop working without warning after updates, and there is no clear way to fix them.
apps.whoFor: Not suitable as a focus timer

apps.title: Limit screen time - Focus lock
apps.verdict: The app changed purpose: it was a hearing test, now it is a screen time control tool. Reviews reflect both periods and do not give an honest picture of current functionality. It cannot be evaluated as a focus tool from the current sample.
apps.loved: Blocking with a minimal limit on useful apps that replaces a bad habit with a good one looks unconventional and interesting.
apps.weak: The app changed its purpose and audience, leaving old users disoriented, and the store reputation does not reflect the actual current product.
apps.whoFor: Hard to define an audience given the app's mixed history

scenarios.name: Student in exam season
scenarios.job: Bank measurable study hours and not slip into the phone when nobody is around to keep watch

scenarios.name: Adult with ADHD
scenarios.job: Support the start and the sequence of the working day with an external structure: a timer, tasks and clear reminders.

scenarios.name: Freelancer billing by the hour
scenarios.job: Record precisely which project the time went to, so the client invoice leaves no room for argument

scenarios.name: Deep work professional
scenarios.job: Disappear into long sessions without interruptions and see at the end of the day how much time was truly focused

scenarios.name: People who want the phone to distract them less often
scenarios.job: Notice the automatic opening of social apps and choose whether to carry on with it now or go back to the task.
